title.zh: 卷376 列傳一百六十三 辛从益 张鳞 顾皋 沈维鐈 朱为 程恩泽 吴杰
title.en: Volume 376 Biographies 163: Xin Congyi, Zhang Lin, Gu Gao, Shen Weiqiao, Zhu Wei, Cheng Enze, Wu Jie
title.raw: 卷376 列傳一百六十三 辛从益 张鳞 顾皋 沈维鐈 朱为 程恩泽 吴杰

sentences.zh: 辛從益，字謙受，江西萬載人。

translations.literal: Xin Congyi, style name Qianshou, was a native of Wanzai in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Congyi, whose style was Qianshou, came from Wanzai in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1790, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，以母​​老陳請終養。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor, and because his mother was old he memorialized requesting leave to retire and care for her until her death.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor but, with an aged mother at home, petitioned for leave to retire and support her in her final years.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十七年，起復補原官。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jiaqing he was recalled to service and restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1812 he was recalled from retirement and reinstated in his former office.

sentences.zh: 會京畿多雨，詔發廩平糶，從益在事，釐剔弊端，實惠及民，時稱之。

translations.literal: At a time when the capital region had heavy rains, an edict ordered grain released from the granaries and sold at fair price; Congyi took part in the work, eliminated abuses, and the benefit reached the people in fact, and he was praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When prolonged rains struck the capital region, the court ordered grain sold from the state granaries at fair price. Congyi took part in the effort, rooted out abuses, and delivered real relief to the people, winning praise at the time.

sentences.zh: 疏請飭督撫詳慎甄別以澄吏治，略曰：「外省甄別，與京員不同​​。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that governors-general and governors conduct careful evaluation with strictness to clarify official administration, stating in summary: "Evaluation in the provinces differs from that of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial urging governors-general and governors to screen officials with greater care so as to purify administration, writing in part: "Provincial evaluation differs from that applied to capital officials.

sentences.zh: 京師耳目甚密，稍有徇私，難逃聖明洞鑑。

translations.literal: In the capital eyes and ears are very numerous; the slightest favoritism cannot escape the Emperor's penetrating scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital scrutiny is intense: the slightest private favor cannot escape the Emperor's penetrating gaze.

sentences.zh: 外省督撫權勢既尊，操縱甚易，豈知州縣有當切責之處，亦有當體恤之處，偏私則是非倒置，刻覈則下情不通。

translations.literal: In the provinces governors-general and governors enjoy exalted authority and manipulation is very easy; how could they know that prefects and magistrates have matters that ought to be sternly reproved and also matters that ought to be treated with consideration—partiality inverts right and wrong, harshness cuts off communication from below.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors-general and governors wield great power and find manipulation easy. They fail to see that prefects and magistrates deserve both sharp rebuke and considerate treatment: partiality inverts right and wrong, while excessive harshness blocks communication from below.

sentences.zh: 臣以為大吏必持廉法之大綱，略趨承之末節；

translations.literal: Your subject holds that high officials must uphold the great principles of integrity and law and set aside the minor points of obsequious compliance;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that senior officials must uphold the great principles of integrity and law, and set aside petty courtesies of obsequious compliance;

sentences.zh: 務幹事之勤能，責安民之實效；

translations.literal: they must value diligence and competence in handling affairs and hold them responsible for the real effect of pacifying the people;
translations.idiomatic: they must value diligence and competence in administration and demand real results in securing the people's welfare;

sentences.zh: 揣時勢之難易，量才分之優絀；

translations.literal: they must gauge the difficulty or ease of the times and measure the superior or inferior allotment of talent;
translations.idiomatic: they must weigh the difficulty of the times and measure each man's allotment of talent, superior or inferior;

sentences.zh: 而又常存敬畏之心，然後能愛惜人才，澄清吏治。」

translations.literal: and moreover constantly preserve a heart of reverent awe—only then can they cherish talent and clarify official administration."
translations.idiomatic: and they must keep a constant heart of reverent awe. Only then can they cherish talent and clarify official administration."

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 十八年，滑縣匪平，軍中多攜養難民子女，從益疏請遣送歸家，如議行，並譴領兵大員。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the bandits in Huaxian were pacified, many in the army had taken along and kept refugee children; Congyi memorialized requesting that they be sent home, and as proposed it was carried out, and the leading officers were also reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813, after the Huaxian rebels were suppressed, many soldiers had taken in refugee children. Congyi memorialized that they be sent home; the court adopted his proposal and also censured the commanding officers.

sentences.zh: 又面奏：「正教昌明，邪說自息，小民不識大義，故易為邪教煽惑。

translations.literal: He also addressed the throne in person: "When orthodox teaching flourishes, heterodox doctrines naturally cease; common people do not understand great principle and are therefore easily incited by heterodox sects.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke to the throne in person: "When orthodox teaching flourishes, heterodox doctrines fade of themselves. Ordinary people lack a grasp of great principle and are easily swayed by heterodox sects.

sentences.zh: 而選人得官，不問風俗淳澆，祗計缺分肥瘠，何以教民？

translations.literal: Yet when selectees receive office they are not asked about whether local custom is pure or corrupt—they only calculate whether the post is fat or lean; how can they teach the people?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when new officials take office no one asks whether local custom is wholesome or corrupt; they reckon only whether the post is lucrative or meager. How can such men teach the people?

sentences.zh: 欲厚風俗，宜先責成牧令。」

translations.literal: If one wishes to improve local custom, one should first hold magistrates and prefects accountable."
translations.idiomatic: If the court wishes to improve local custom, it should first hold magistrates and prefects accountable."

sentences.zh: 歷光祿寺少卿、通政司參議、內閣侍讀學士、光祿寺卿、太常寺卿。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, counsellor of the Office of Transmission, reader in the Grand Secretariat, minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and minister of the Court of Imperial Music.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, counsellor of the Office of Transmission, reader in the Grand Secretariat, minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and minister of the Court of Imperial Music.

sentences.zh: 道光初，山西學政陳官俊鐫級回京，仍直上書房，從益疏劾曰：「上書房為教冑諭德之地，視學政為尤重，宜慎選德行敦厚、器識宏達之儒臣，使皇子有所觀法，薰陶養其德性。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang, Chen Guanjun, educational commissioner of Shanxi, was demoted in rank and returned to the capital yet still entered the Upper Study Hall; Congyi memorialized in impeachment, saying: "The Upper Study Hall is the place for instructing the heir apparent and tutoring the sons of the Emperor, and is even weightier than the post of educational commissioner; one should carefully select Confucian officials of solid virtue and broad capacity, so that the princes have models to observe and may be nurtured and their moral nature cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign Chen Guanjun, former educational commissioner of Shanxi, was demoted yet still entered the Upper Study Hall. Congyi impeached him, writing: "The Upper Study Hall instructs the heir apparent and tutors the imperial sons—a charge weightier even than provincial educational commissioner. The court should choose Confucian officials of solid virtue and broad capacity so that the princes have models to follow and their moral nature may be cultivated.

sentences.zh: 陳官俊在學政任，不能遠色避嫌，懲忿窒慾，性行之駁，器識之褊，不宜仍居授讀之任。」

translations.literal: Chen Guanjun in his term as educational commissioner could not keep distant from beauty and avoid suspicion, restrain anger and choke off desire; the flaws in his conduct and the narrowness of his capacity make him unfit to remain in the post of lecturing and reading."
translations.idiomatic: During his term as educational commissioner Chen Guanjun failed to keep his distance from beauty and avoid suspicion, or to restrain anger and curb desire. The flaws in his conduct and the narrowness of his capacity make him unfit to continue lecturing the princes."

sentences.zh: 二年，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 宣宗溫諭曰：「爾甚朴忠，無所希冀，亦無所揣摩。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor gave him a warm instruction, saying: "You are very plain and loyal, without hope or calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong addressed him warmly: "You are thoroughly plain and loyal, without hope or calculation.

sentences.zh: 有所聞見，直言無隱，朕無忌諱也。」

translations.literal: Whatever you hear or see, speak frankly without concealment; I have no taboos."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever you hear or observe, speak frankly without concealment. I harbor no taboos."

sentences.zh: 命偕尚書文孚赴陝西讞獄。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go with Minister Wen Fu to Shaanxi to try cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to accompany Minister Wen Fu to Shaanxi to hear criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 渭南富民柳全璧殺其傭硃錫林，賄知縣徐潤得免死，巡撫硃勳庇之，獄久不決。

translations.literal: The wealthy commoner Liu Quanbi of Weinan killed his hired man Zhu Xilin, bribed the magistrate Xu Run to escape the death penalty, and the governor Zhu Xun shielded him, so the case long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quanbi, a wealthy man of Weinan, murdered his hired laborer Zhu Xilin. He bribed Magistrate Xu Run to escape execution, and Governor Zhu Xun shielded him, so the case dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 從益等鞫得其狀，論如法。

translations.literal: Congyi and the others examined and obtained the facts, and sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi and his colleagues examined the facts and sentenced the parties according to law.

sentences.zh: 覆命，陳陝西馬政之害，地方官春秋計裡買馬，實則民不得直，而官亦不需馬，第指馬索賕以為民病，請禁革。

translations.literal: On reporting back, he stated the harm of Shaanxi horse administration: local officials in spring and autumn nominally purchased horses by the li, but in fact the people received no fair price while the officials also had no need of horses—they merely designated horses and demanded bribes as a affliction on the people, and he requested prohibition and abolition.
translations.idiomatic: On reporting back he described abuses in Shaanxi horse administration: local officials each spring and autumn nominally purchased horses by the li, yet the people received no fair price while officials needed no horses at all—they merely designated horses and extorted bribes, a plague on the people. He requested that the practice be banned and abolished.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢禮部侍郎，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to vice minister of Rites and appointed educational commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 he was promoted to vice minister of Rites and appointed educational commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 於是巡撫陶澍奏禁紳衿包漕，橫索漕規，下學政稽查懲治。

translations.literal: Thereupon Governor Tao Shu memorialized prohibiting gentry and licentiates from monopolizing grain transport and extorting transport fees, and ordered the educational commissioner to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tao Shu then memorialized to prohibit gentry and licentiates from monopolizing grain transport and extorting transport fees, directing the educational commissioner to investigate and punish offenders.

sentences.zh: 從益上疏曰：「江蘇漕額本重，豈堪浮收無節？

translations.literal: Congyi memorialized upward, saying: "Jiangsu's grain transport quota is already heavy—how can it bear unchecked over-collection?
translations.idiomatic: Congyi memorialized: "Jiangsu's grain transport quota is already heavy. How can it bear unchecked over-collection?

sentences.zh: 州縣自應調劑，閭閻尤宜體恤。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates ought themselves to adjust matters, and among the lanes and alleys the people especially ought to receive consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates should make adjustments themselves, and common households especially deserve consideration.

sentences.zh: 久懸定額，尚肆苛求；

translations.literal: When the fixed quota has long been suspended, they still extort without restraint;
translations.idiomatic: Even when the fixed quota has long gone uncollected, officials still extort without restraint;

sentences.zh: 明語浮收，必滋流弊。

translations.literal: to speak openly of over-collection will surely breed further abuses.
translations.idiomatic: to speak openly of permitting over-collection will surely breed further abuses.

sentences.zh: 撫臣之意，謂控漕之人即包漕之人，臣以為未必盡然。

translations.literal: The governor's intention is that those who lodge complaints about transport are themselves those who monopolize transport; your subject holds that this is not necessarily entirely so.
translations.idiomatic: The governor holds that anyone who lodges complaints about transport must be a transport monopolist himself. I hold that this is not necessarily so.

sentences.zh: 官之收漕，必用吏役，吏役貪狠，必圖肥己。

translations.literal: When officials collect transport tax they must use clerks and runners; clerks and runners are greedy and fierce and must seek to enrich themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Officials collecting transport grain must employ clerks and runners, who are greedy and ruthless and invariably seek their own profit.

sentences.zh: 官既浮收，吏又朘削，不特小民受害，即循謹生監，亦被其累，激而上控，此中固有不得已者。

translations.literal: When officials over-collect, clerks again pare away, so that not only do common people suffer but even cautious licentiates are burdened by them and in exasperation appeal upward—among these there are indeed those who have no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: When officials over-collect, clerks skim yet again. Small households suffer, but even cautious licentiates are caught in the net and, driven to desperation, appeal to higher authority—among them are men who truly have no other recourse.

sentences.zh: 撫臣又稱生監需索漕規，地方官費無所出，乃取償於純謹小民。

translations.literal: The governor also said that licentiates demand transport fees and that local officials, having nowhere to meet the expense, recover it from honest common people.
translations.idiomatic: The governor also claims that licentiates demand transport fees and that local officials, unable to cover the cost, recoup it from honest common people.

sentences.zh: 臣伏思吏役貪得無厭，縱生監悉循循守法，而小民追呼徵比之煩，亦斷不能為之少減。

translations.literal: Your subject reflects that clerks and runners are insatiably greedy; even if every licentiate were utterly law-abiding, the people's trouble from summonses and forced collection could by no means be reduced even slightly.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that clerks and runners are insatiably greedy. Even if every licentiate obeyed the law to the letter, the people's torment from summonses and forced collection would not lessen in the slightest.

sentences.zh: 吏役倚官府為城社，倘違例浮收，無人控訴，將何術以治之？

translations.literal: Clerks and runners rely on the yamen as their stronghold; if they over-collect in violation of regulations and no one lodges complaint, by what means can they be governed?
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and runners treat the yamen as their fortress. If they over-collect in violation of statute and no one dares complain, by what means can they be governed?

sentences.zh: 夫劣衿律所不宥，苛政亦法所必裁。

translations.literal: Worthless licentiates the law does not pardon, and harsh government the law also must cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Worthless licentiates the law does not spare, and harsh government the law must also restrain.

sentences.zh: 矯枉勢必過正，創法宜防流弊。

translations.literal: To straighten the crooked the effort must go too far, and when creating regulations one should guard against abuses.
translations.idiomatic: In straightening what is crooked the effort inevitably overshoots; in framing new rules one must guard against unintended abuse.

sentences.zh: 管見所及，不敢不以上聞。」

translations.literal: What this humble view reaches, I dare not fail to report upward."
translations.idiomatic: What my humble view reaches, I dare not withhold from Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 從益廉靜坦白，遇非理必爭，不為權要詘。

translations.literal: Congyi was pure, quiet, and frank; when he encountered what was unreasonable he was sure to contend and would not yield to powerful persons.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was upright, quiet, and candid. When he met injustice he contested it and would not bow to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒於學政任所。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at his educational commissioner's post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1828 he died at his post as educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 著有奏疏、詩文內外集、公孫龍子注。

translations.literal: He authored collected memorials, poetry and prose in inner and outer collections, and a commentary on Gongsun Longzi.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected memorials, inner and outer collections of poetry and prose, and a commentary on the Gongsun Longzi.

sentences.zh: 張鱗，字小軒，浙江長興人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin, style name Xiaoxuan, was a native of Changxing in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin, whose style was Xiaoxuan, came from Changxing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1799 and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 習國書，授檢討。

translations.literal: He studied the national language and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Manchu language and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 仁宗臨幸翰林院，鱗獻詩冊，被恩賚。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, Lin presented a poetry album and received imperial favor and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong visited the Hanlin Academy, Lin presented a volume of poetry and received imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 十七年，大考二等，遷贊善。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, in the great examination he placed second class and was transferred to tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1812, in the triennial evaluation he placed in the second class and was promoted to tutor.

sentences.zh: 歷侍講、庶子。

translations.literal: He served successively as lecturer and junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as lecturer and junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 二十年，選翰林官入直懋勤殿，纂輯秘殿珠林、石渠寶笈，鱗與焉。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was chosen as a Hanlin official to enter duty at the Maojin Hall and compile the Secret Hall Pearl Forest and the Stone Canal Precious Collection; Lin was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1815 he was selected as a Hanlin official for duty at the Maojin Hall to compile the Secret Hall Pearl Forest and the Stone Canal Precious Collection; Lin took part.

sentences.zh: 歷侍講學士、國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: He served successively as lecturing academician and director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as lecturing academician and director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，典江西鄉試。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1819 he presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 尋以齋戒未至齋所，降授太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because during the fasting period he had not reached the fasting lodge, he was demoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Music.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, because he failed to reach the fasting lodge during the abstention period, he was demoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Music.

sentences.zh: 遷通政使司副使、太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission and minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission and minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，命偕太常寺少卿明安泰赴楊村挑驗​​剝船，遂赴東光、盧龍兩縣訊鞫京控獄，各論如律；

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was ordered to go with Vice Minister Ming Antai of the Court of Imperial Music to Yangcun to inspect stripped transport boats, and then proceeded to Dongguang and Lulong to examine and try capital-appeal cases, each sentenced according to law;
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was ordered with Vice Minister Ming Antai of the Court of Imperial Music to Yangcun to inspect stripped transport boats, then proceeded to Dongguang and Lulong to hear capital appeals, sentencing each case according to law;

sentences.zh: 並劾承審官濫刑，巡道徇庇，褫黜有差。

translations.literal: he also impeached the trial officials for excessive punishment and the circuit intendant for partial shielding, and dismissals and demotions were meted out in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: he also impeached trial officials for excessive punishment and a circuit intendant for partial shielding, and dismissals and demotions followed in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉太常寺卿，督安徽學政，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to minister of the Court of Imperial Music, appointed educational commissioner of Anhui, and promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 he became minister of the Court of Imperial Music, was appointed educational commissioner of Anhui, and was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 七年，以繼母憂歸，服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he returned home on mourning for his stepmother; when the mourning period ended he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1827 he returned home to mourn his stepmother; when the mourning ended he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部侍郎，督福建學政。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of War and appointed educational commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of War and appointed educational commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十三年，補戶部，又調吏部。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and then to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1833 he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and then to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 福建縣丞秦師韓控訐總督程祖洛，侍郎趙盛奎偕鱗同案鞫，白其誣，師韓遣戍。

translations.literal: The Fujian county assistant Qin Shihan lodged accusations against Governor Cheng Zuluo; Vice Minister Zhao Shengkui together with Lin jointly examined the case, cleared him of the false charges, and Qin Shihan was sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: County Assistant Qin Shihan of Fujian accused Governor Cheng Zuluo. Vice Minister Zhao Shengkui and Lin jointly heard the case, cleared the governor of the false charges, and sent Qin Shihan into exile.

sentences.zh: 鱗清廉儉素，杜絕乾謁。

translations.literal: Lin was pure, incorrupt, and frugal, and cut off all improper solicitations.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was upright, incorruptible, and frugal, and refused all improper solicitations.

sentences.zh: 兩為學政，卻陋規，拔寒畯，閩人尤頌之。

translations.literal: Twice serving as educational commissioner, he rejected customary fees, promoted poor scholars of talent, and the people of Fujian especially praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Twice serving as educational commissioner, he rejected customary fees and elevated poor scholars of talent; the people of Fujian praised him especially.

sentences.zh: 衡文力矯通榜之習。

translations.literal: In evaluating examination papers he strove to correct the habit of mutual favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: In grading examination papers he worked hard to correct the habit of mutual favoritism.

sentences.zh: 十五年，典會試，以校閱勞致疾，出闈，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he presided over the metropolitan examination; from the labor of proofreading he fell ill, and after leaving the examination compound he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he presided over the metropolitan examination. The strain of proofreading brought on illness, and he died after leaving the examination compound.

sentences.zh: 福建士民請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Fujian scholars and common people requested that he be enshrined in the shrine of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian scholars and commoners petitioned to enshrine him in the shrine of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 顧皋，字歅齊，江蘇無錫人。

translations.literal: Gu Gao, style name Yinqi, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Gao, whose style was Yinqi, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he placed first in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he ranked first in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 九年，督貴州學政，釐剔弊竇，奏改黎平、開泰學額，士林頌之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed educational commissioner of Guizhou, eliminated abuses, memorialized to alter the examination quotas of Liping and Kaitai, and the scholarly community praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1804 he was appointed educational commissioner of Guizhou, eliminated abuses, memorialized to revise the examination quotas of Liping and Kaitai, and won praise from the scholarly community.

sentences.zh: 超擢國子監司業。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to director of studies of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to director of studies of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，直懋勤殿，編輯秘殿珠林、石渠寶笈。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he entered duty at the Maojin Hall and compiled the Secret Hall Pearl Forest and the Stone Canal Precious Collection.
translations.idiomatic: In 1816 he took duty at the Maojin Hall and compiled the Secret Hall Pearl Forest and the Stone Canal Precious Collection.

sentences.zh: 歷翰林院侍讀、左右庶子、侍講學士、侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He served successively as reader of the Hanlin Academy, left and right junior tutor, lecturing academician, and reading academician.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Hanlin reader, left and right junior tutor, lecturing academician, and reading academician.

sentences.zh: 典陝甘鄉試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，入直上書房，甚被仁宗眷注。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he entered the Upper Study Hall and was greatly favored and noted by the Renzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1819 he entered the Upper Study Hall and won great favor from Emperor Renzong.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，扈蹕熱河。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In 1820 he accompanied the court to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 上升遐之日，御筆擢皋詹事。

translations.literal: On the day the late Emperor ascended to the Highest, by his own brush he promoted Gao to junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the late Emperor passed away, he personally promoted Gao to junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 次日，宣宗即位，執皋手大慟。

translations.literal: The next day, when the Xuanzong Emperor took the throne, he grasped Gao's hand and wept greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he took Gao's hand and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，遷內閣學士，擢工部侍郎，兼管錢法堂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to Grand Secretariat academician, promoted to vice minister of Works, and concurrently managed the Bureau of Currency.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician and vice minister of Works, and concurrently managed the Bureau of Currency.

sentences.zh: 二年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 連典順天、浙江鄉試，管理國子監事務。

translations.literal: He presided in succession over the Shuntian and Zhejiang provincial examinations and managed the affairs of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He presided in succession over the Shuntian and Zhejiang provincial examinations and managed the affairs of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 皋在戶部，不為激亢之行，考覈利病，慎稽出納，不可干以私。

translations.literal: When Gao was at the Ministry of Revenue he did not act in an inflammatory manner; he examined benefits and harms, carefully checked receipts and disbursements, and could not be swayed by private interest.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Revenue Gao avoided inflammatory conduct. He weighed benefits and harms, carefully audited receipts and disbursements, and could not be moved by private interest.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「學期見諸實用。

translations.literal: He once said: "Learning should be realized in practical use.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Learning ought to be put to practical use.

sentences.zh: 吾久迴翔於文學侍從。

translations.literal: I have long hovered in literary attendance on the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: I have long lingered in literary attendance upon the throne.

sentences.zh: 及任經世理物之責，未能壹志專慮，以求稱職，為自愧耳。」

translations.literal: Now that I bear the responsibility of ordering the world and managing things, I have been unable to devote my whole mind and concentrate my thought to seek to fulfill my office, and this is my own shame."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I bear responsibility for ordering the world and managing affairs, I have not been able to devote my whole mind to fulfilling my charge, and that is my shame."

sentences.zh: 八年，以病乞歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he requested leave to return home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1828 he requested leave to return home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1831 he died.

sentences.zh: 沈維鐈，字子彝，浙江嘉興人。

translations.literal: Shen Weiqiao, style name Ziyi, was a native of Jiaxing in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Weiqiao, whose style was Ziyi, came from Jiaxing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he earned his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷司業、洗馬。

translations.literal: He served successively as director of studies and groom-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as director of studies and groom-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 與修全唐文、西巡盛典、一統志，入直懋勤殿，纂輯秘殿珠林、石渠寶笈。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Complete Tang Prose, the Western Tour Ceremonial Record, and the Unified Gazetteer, entered duty at the Maojin Hall, and compiled the Secret Hall Pearl Forest and the Stone Canal Precious Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Complete Tang Prose, the Western Tour Ceremonial Record, and the Unified Gazetteer, took duty at the Maojin Hall, and compiled the Secret Hall Pearl Forest and the Stone Canal Precious Collection.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，督湖北學政，禁習邪教，以端士風。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed educational commissioner of Hubei, prohibited study of heterodox sects, and thereby rectified scholarly custom.
translations.idiomatic: In 1816 he was appointed educational commissioner of Hubei, prohibited study of heterodox sects, and thereby rectified scholarly custom.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to lecturing academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to lecturing academician.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，典福建鄉試，留學政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he presided over the Fujian provincial examination and remained as educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he presided over the Fujian provincial examination and remained as educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 疏陳州縣私設班館之弊，請飭嚴禁，並禁監生充緝捕、催科諸役。

translations.literal: He memorialized stating the abuse of prefects and magistrates privately establishing class halls, requesting strict prohibition, and also prohibiting supervising students from serving as arresters, tax collectors, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the abuse of prefects and magistrates maintaining private tutoring halls, requesting strict prohibition, and also forbade supervising students from serving as arresters, tax collectors, and similar roles.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 八年，督順天學政，轉太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed educational commissioner of Shuntian and transferred to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In 1828 he was appointed educational commissioner of Shuntian and transferred to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 任滿，遷宗人府丞，署副都御史，尋實授。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was transferred to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, acted as vice censor-in-chief, and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was promoted to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, served as acting vice censor-in-chief, and soon received substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 十二年，督安徽學政，奏請增建壽州考棚，與鳳陽分試。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed educational commissioner of Anhui and memorialized requesting additional construction of examination sheds at Shouzhou, with separate examinations from Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he was appointed educational commissioner of Anhui and memorialized to build additional examination sheds at Shouzhou so that candidates there could be examined separately from Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 瀕江水災，偕疆吏會籌賑撫，士民頌之。

translations.literal: When floods struck along the river he joined frontier officials in planning relief and comfort, and scholars and common people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck the river districts he joined frontier officials in planning relief, and scholars and commoners praised him.

sentences.zh: 維鐈居官廉，屢視學，所至弊絕風清，振拔多知名士，宣宗知之，期滿連任。

translations.literal: Weiqiao in office was incorrupt; repeatedly inspecting education, wherever he went abuses ceased and custom was purified, and he elevated many well-known scholars; the Xuanzong Emperor knew him, and when his term ended he was reappointed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqiao served with integrity. On repeated tours as educational commissioner he cleared abuses wherever he went, elevated many renowned scholars, and won notice from Emperor Xuanzong, who reappointed him when his term ended.

sentences.zh: 擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十七年，請回籍營葬，詔予假三月，毋庸開缺，事竣回京。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he requested leave to return home to arrange burial; an edict granted three months' leave without vacating his post, and when the matter was finished he was to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he requested leave to return home for burial. The court granted three months without vacating his post, with orders to return to the capital when the rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以耳疾許免職，命病痊以聞。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, on account of ear ailment he was permitted to resign; he was ordered to report when his illness recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838, suffering from ear trouble, he was permitted to resign, with orders to report when he recovered.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒於家。

translations.literal: The following year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 維鐈學以宋儒為歸，謂典章制度與夫聲音訓詁當宗漢人，而道理則備於程、硃，務為身心有用之學。

translations.literal: Weiqiao in learning took Song Confucians as his goal, holding that institutions and regulations together with phonology and exegesis should follow the Han scholars, while principle was fully provided in Cheng and Zhu, and he strove for learning useful to body and mind.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqiao took the Song Confucians as his standard. He held that institutions and phonological exegesis should follow Han scholarship, while moral principle was fully articulated by Cheng and Zhu, and he pursued learning of real use to body and mind.

sentences.zh: 校刊宋儒諸書以教士，時稱其醇謹焉。

translations.literal: He collated and published various books of Song Confucians to instruct scholars, and at the time he was praised for his pure carefulness.
translations.idiomatic: He collated and published works of Song Confucians to instruct scholars, and was praised at the time for his sober integrity.

sentences.zh: 祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: He was enshrined in the local worthies' shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the local worthies' shrine.

sentences.zh: 朱為弼，字右甫，浙江平湖人。

translations.literal: Zhu Weibi, style name Youfu, was a native of Pinghu in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Weibi, whose style was Youfu, came from Pinghu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年進士，授兵部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of War, and was transferred to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he earned his jinshi degree, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of War, and was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，授御史，遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was appointed censor and transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was appointed censor and promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏請整頓京師緝捕，劾倉場覆奏海運倉豆石霉變情形不實，命大臣按鞫，侍郎和桂、張映漢並被譴。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting rectification of capital arrest and pursuit, impeached the grain depot for reporting untruly on the condition of moldy beans and grain in the sea-transport granaries, and the court ordered grand ministers to examine and try; Vice Ministers He Gui and Zhang Yinghan were both reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to tighten capital policing, impeached the grain depot for misreporting mold in sea-transport granaries, and the court ordered grand ministers to investigate. Vice Ministers He Gui and Zhang Yinghan were both censured.

sentences.zh: 又疏陳江蘇海口壅塞，浙江上游均受其害，請疏濬太湖下游劉河、吳淞諸水，為一勞永逸之計，如所議行。

translations.literal: He also memorialized stating that the Jiangsu estuary was blocked and upstream Zhejiang suffered equally, requesting dredging of the Liu River, Wusong, and other waters below Lake Tai as a plan for lasting benefit, and as proposed it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that the Jiangsu estuary was silted and upstream Zhejiang suffered equally, requesting dredging of the Liu River, Wusong, and other channels below Lake Tai as a lasting remedy. The court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢順天府府丞，遷府尹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to vice director of Shuntian Prefecture and transferred to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he was promoted to vice director of Shuntian Prefecture and then to prefect.

sentences.zh: 有蝗孽，單騎馳視，卻屬官供張，曰：「吾為蝗來，乃以我為蝗耶？」

translations.literal: When locusts appeared he rode alone on a fast horse to inspect, but rejected the lavish reception prepared by subordinate officials, saying: "I came for the locusts—are you treating me as a locust?"
translations.idiomatic: When locusts appeared he rode out alone to inspect the damage, but refused the lavish reception his subordinates prepared, saying, "I came for the locusts—are you treating me as one?"

sentences.zh: 六年，复降授府丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again demoted to vice director of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was again demoted to vice director of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷通政司副使、太常寺卿、宗人府府丞、都察院左副都御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, minister of the Court of Imperial Music, director of the Imperial Clan Court, and left vice censor-in-chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, minister of the Court of Imperial Music, director of the Imperial Clan Court, and left vice censor-in-chief of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢兵部侍郎，權倉場侍郎，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to vice minister of War, acted as vice minister of the grain depot, and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1833 he was promoted to vice minister of War, acted as vice minister of the grain depot, and soon received substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 十四年，出為漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out as director-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In 1834 he was appointed director-general of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 時漕船水手恣橫，廬州幫在東昌械鬥，傷斃多命，下為弼查辦，疏言：「漕督例隨幫尾，在前者無從遙制。

translations.literal: At the time transport-boat sailors were overbearing; the Luzhou gang fought with weapons at Dongchang and many were wounded or killed; the case was sent down to Weibi to investigate and try, and he memorialized, saying: "The transport director by custom follows the tail of the gang; those ahead cannot be controlled from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Transport sailors had grown overbearing. The Luzhou gang fought at Dongchang, leaving many dead and wounded. The case was assigned to Weibi, who memorialized: "The transport director customarily follows the rear of a convoy and cannot control boats ahead from a distance.

sentences.zh: 請責成押運官弁會同地方官拏辦。」

translations.literal: He requested that escort officers and local officials be held responsible jointly to arrest and try offenders."
translations.idiomatic: He requested that grain escort officers and local officials be held jointly responsible for arresting and trying offenders."

sentences.zh: 並定頭柁十家聯保，舉發徇隱賞懲之法，奏陳剔弊速漕章程八事，下所司議行。

translations.literal: He also fixed a system of joint guarantee among ten head-boat families, with rewards and punishments for reporting or concealing, memorialized eight regulations for eliminating abuses and speeding transport, and these were sent down to the relevant offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also instituted joint guarantee among ten head-boat families, with rewards and penalties for reporting or concealing violations, and memorialized eight regulations to eliminate abuses and speed transport. These were referred to the relevant offices for implementation.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以病乞免，允之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he requested leave on account of illness and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he requested leave on account of illness and was granted it.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1840 he died.

sentences.zh: 為弼精揅金石之學，佐阮元纂鐘鼎彝器款識，所著有蕉聲館詩文集。

translations.literal: Weibi was expert in the study of bronze and stone; he assisted Ruan Yuan in compiling inscriptions on bells, tripods, and ritual vessels, and his authored works include the Poetry and Prose Collection of the Plantain Sound Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Weibi was an expert in epigraphy and assisted Ruan Yuan in compiling inscriptions on bronze ritual vessels. His works include the Poetry and Prose Collection of the Plantain Sound Hall.

sentences.zh: 程恩澤，字春海，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: Cheng Enze, style name Chunhai, was a native of She County in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Enze, whose style was Chunhai, came from She County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 父昌期，乾隆四十五年一甲三名進士，累官至侍講學士，直上書房。

translations.literal: His father Changqi, in the forty-fifth year of Qianlong placed third in the top tier of the jinshi examination, rose through offices to lecturing academician, and entered the Upper Study Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His father Changqi ranked third in the top tier of the jinshi examination in 1780, rose to lecturing academician, and entered the Upper Study Hall.

sentences.zh: 恩澤勤學嗜奇，受經於江都凌廷堪，廷堪勗之曰：「學必天人並至，博而能精，所成乃大。」

translations.literal: Enze studied diligently and loved the unusual; he received the classics from Ling Tingkan of Jiangdu, and Tingkan exhorted him, saying: "Learning must reach both Heaven and man, be broad yet able to be refined—only then is one's achievement great."
translations.idiomatic: Enze studied diligently and loved the recondite. He studied the classics under Ling Tingkan of Jiangdu, who exhorted him: "Learning must unite Heaven and man, be broad yet refined—only then is one's achievement great."

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十六年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1811 he earned his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，入直南書房，宣宗曰：「汝父蘭翹先生昔年在上書房，朕敬其品學。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he entered duty at the Southern Study Hall; the Xuanzong Emperor said: "Your father Mr. Lanqiao in former years was in the Upper Study Hall, and I respected his character and learning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he entered duty at the Southern Study Hall. Emperor Xuanzong said: "Your father Mr. Lanqiao once served in the Upper Study Hall, and I respected his character and learning.

sentences.zh: 汝之聲名，亦所深悉，宜更守素行。」

translations.literal: Your reputation also is deeply known to me; you should still more preserve your plain conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Your reputation is also well known to me. You must preserve your plain conduct all the more."

sentences.zh: 典試四川。

translations.literal: He presided over the Sichuan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Sichuan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 三年，督貴州學政，勸民育栗蠶，其利大行。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed educational commissioner of Guizhou, urged the people to raise chestnut silkworms, and the benefit spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 he was appointed educational commissioner of Guizhou, urged the people to raise chestnut silkworms, and the practice spread widely.

sentences.zh: 重刊岳珂五經以訓士。

translations.literal: He reprinted Yue Ke's Five Classics to instruct scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He reprinted Yue Ke's edition of the Five Classics to instruct scholars.

sentences.zh: 鄭珍有異才，特優異之，餉以學，卒為碩儒。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhen had unusual talent; he especially favored and distinguished him, supplied him for study, and in the end he became a great scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhen possessed unusual talent. Enze favored him especially, supported his studies, and Zheng in the end became a great scholar.

sentences.zh: 六年，調湖南學政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to educational commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was transferred to educational commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 任滿回京，洊擢國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital and was repeatedly promoted to director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to the capital and was repeatedly promoted, becoming director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 命充春秋左傳纂修官，推本賈、服，不守杜氏一家之言。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as compiler of the Spring and Autumn Zuo Commentary, tracing back to Jia and Fu and not adhering to the Du clan alone.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed compiler of the Spring and Autumn Zuo Commentary, tracing back to Jia Kui and Fu Qian rather than adhering to Du Yu alone.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 十一年，服闋，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when mourning ended, he still entered duty at the Southern Study Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In 1831, when mourning ended, he resumed duty at the Southern Study Hall.

sentences.zh: 未補官，特命典試廣東。

translations.literal: Before he was restored to office he was specially ordered to preside over the Guangdong examination.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was restored to regular office he was specially ordered to preside over the Guangdong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 知南海曾釗名，冀得之。

translations.literal: Knowing Zeng Zhao of Nanhai by reputation, he hoped to obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Zeng Zhao of Nanhai by reputation, he hoped to place him on the list.

sentences.zh: 釗未與試，榜發，大失望。

translations.literal: Zhao did not take the examination; when the list was published, he was greatly disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng did not sit for the examination. When the list was published, Enze was deeply disappointed.

sentences.zh: 所得多知名士。

translations.literal: Those he obtained were mostly well-known scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Those he did select were mostly well-known scholars.

sentences.zh: 改直上書房，授惠親王讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Upper Study Hall and instructed Prince Hui in reading.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Upper Study Hall and instructed Prince Hui in reading.

sentences.zh: 遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授工部侍郎，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed vice minister of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1834 he was appointed vice minister of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以部務繁，罷直書房。

translations.literal: Because ministry affairs were numerous, he ceased duty at the Study Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Because ministry affairs were heavy, he ceased duty at the Study Hall.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒，上甚惜之，優詔賜卹，賜其子德威舉人。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died; the Emperor greatly regretted it, granted favorable edict and condolence gifts, and granted his son Dewei the rank of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he died. The Emperor deeply regretted his loss, granted a favorable edict and condolence gifts, and conferred on his son Dewei the rank of provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 恩澤博聞強識，於六藝九流皆深思心知其意，天象、地輿、壬遁、太乙、脈經莫不窮究。

translations.literal: Enze was broadly learned and strong in memory; of the Six Arts and Nine Schools he pondered deeply and knew their meaning in his heart; celestial phenomena, geography, renda, taiyi, and medical classics—none did he fail to investigate exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: Enze was broadly learned with a powerful memory. Of the Six Arts and Nine Schools he pondered deeply until he knew their meaning by heart. Celestial phenomena, geography, renda divination, taiyi numerology, and medical classics—none escaped exhaustive study.

sentences.zh: 謂近人治算，由九章以通四元，可謂發明絕學，而儀器則罕傳，欲修復古儀器而未果。

translations.literal: He said that recent men in mathematics, proceeding from the Nine Chapters to master the four elements, could be called to have opened supreme learning, yet instruments were rarely transmitted; he wished to restore ancient instruments but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He held that recent mathematicians, advancing from the Nine Chapters to master the four elements, had opened supreme learning, yet instruments were rarely transmitted. He wished to restore ancient instruments but did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 詩古文辭皆深雅。

translations.literal: His poetry and classical prose were all profound and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and classical prose were all profound and elegant.

sentences.zh: 時乾、嘉宿儒多徂謝，惟大學士阮元為士林尊仰，恩澤名位亞於元，為足繼之。

translations.literal: At the time many Qianlong and Jiaqing elder scholars had passed away; only Grand Secretary Ruan Yuan was honored and looked up to by the scholarly community, and Enze in fame and rank was next to Yuan, sufficient to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: By then many elder scholars of the Qianlong and Jiaqing eras had passed away. Only Grand Secretary Ruan Yuan still commanded the scholarly world's respect, and Enze in fame and rank stood next to Ruan, fit to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 所欲著書多未成，惟國策地名考二十卷、詩文集十卷傳於世。

translations.literal: Most of the books he wished to write were unfinished; only the twenty-juan Investigation of Place Names in the Strategies of the Warring States and the ten-juan collected writings were transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the books he planned remained unfinished. Only his twenty-juan Investigation of Place Names in the Strategies of the Warring States and his ten-juan collected writings survive.

sentences.zh: 吳杰，字梅梁，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Wu Jie, style name Meiliang, was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie, whose style was Meiliang, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少能文，為阮元所知。

translations.literal: In youth he could write; he was known to Ruan Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he could write well and came to Ruan Yuan's notice.

sentences.zh: 以拔貢生應天津召試，二等，充文穎館謄錄，書成，授昌化教諭。

translations.literal: As a selected tribute student he responded to the Tianjin imperial summons examination, placed second class, served as copyist of the Wenyin Hall, and when the book was finished was appointed instructor of Changhua.
translations.idiomatic: As a selected tribute student he took the Tianjin imperial summons examination, placed in the second class, served as copyist of the Wenyin Hall, and when the compilation was finished was appointed instructor of Changhua.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1814 he earned his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，督四川學政，疏請以唐陸贄從祀文廟，下部議行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was appointed educational commissioner of Sichuan and memorialized requesting that Tang Lu Zhi be admitted to the Confucian temple sacrifices; the ministry deliberated and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was appointed educational commissioner of Sichuan and memorialized that the Tang statesman Lu Zhi be admitted to the Confucian temple sacrifices. The ministry deliberated and approved.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，出為湖南嶽常澧道，歷貴州按察使、順天府丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary, went out as intendant of Yue-Chang-Li in Hunan, and served successively as judicial commissioner of Guizhou and vice director of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary, then served as intendant of Yue-Chang-Li in Hunan, and in succession as judicial commissioner of Guizhou and vice director of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十三年，川南叛夷犯邊，師久無功，傑疏言：「川夷作亂，提督桂涵連戰克捷，生擒首逆，清溪近邊遂無夷。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year rebel Yi in southern Sichuan raided the border; the army long had no success; Jie memorialized, saying: "When the Sichuan Yi rebelled, Regional Commander Gui Han won successive battles and captured the rebel leader alive; near Qingxi on the border there were soon no Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1833 rebel Yi in southern Sichuan raided the frontier. The campaign dragged on without success. Jie memorialized: "When the Sichuan Yi rebelled, Regional Commander Gui Han won successive victories and captured the rebel leader alive, and the Qingxi frontier was soon cleared of Yi.

sentences.zh: 楊芳繼任，用兵之區僅瓘邊一處，夷寇不過數部落，當易獲勝。

translations.literal: Yang Fang succeeded to command; the area of military operations was only the single place of Zhanbian; the Yi raiders were no more than several tribes—it ought to be easy to obtain victory.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang succeeded him in command. The theater of war was only the Zhanbian sector, and the Yi raiders numbered no more than a few tribes—victory ought to have been easy.

sentences.zh: 惟夷巢跬步皆山，夏令河水盛漲，徒涉尤難。

translations.literal: Only the Yi nests at every step are mountains; in summer when river water swells, crossing on foot is especially difficult.
translations.idiomatic: But Yi strongholds lie in mountains at every step, and in summer when rivers swell, crossing on foot is especially difficult.

sentences.zh: 楊芳自抵瓘邊，頓兵三月。

translations.literal: Yang Fang from the time he reached Zhanbian halted the army for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang, from the day he reached Zhanbian, halted the army for three months.

sentences.zh: 臣思其故，必逆夷退伏老巢，水潦既降，不易深入。

translations.literal: Your subject considers the reason: the rebellious Yi must have retreated to their old nests; once the floods subsided it would not be easy to penetrate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: I consider the reason: the rebellious Yi had retreated to their old strongholds. Once the floods subsided, deep penetration would not be easy.

sentences.zh: 楊芳不敢以軍情入告，但稱督兵進剿，實皆游移觀望之辭。

translations.literal: Yang Fang dared not report the military situation upward but only said he was supervising troops in pursuit—in fact these were all words of hesitation and watchful waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang dared not report the true military situation, claiming only that he was leading troops in pursuit—in fact these were words of hesitation and watchful waiting.

sentences.zh: 曠日持久，邊事所關非細，請敕總督鄂山體察確奏，毋得徇隱。」

translations.literal: Days and months prolonged—the border affair concerns no small matter; I request an edict to Governor E Shan to investigate and report accurately, and not to shield anyone."
translations.idiomatic: The campaign drags on day after day, and frontier affairs are no small matter. I request that Governor E Shan investigate and report accurately, without shielding anyone."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「馭夷長策，當先剿後撫。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, saying: "The long-term policy for governing Yi is to pacify only after exterminating.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "The long-term policy for governing Yi is to pacify only after exterminating.

sentences.zh: 未剿遽撫，良莠不分。

translations.literal: To pacify before exterminating is to fail to distinguish good from bad.
translations.idiomatic: To pacify before exterminating fails to distinguish good from bad.

sentences.zh: 兵至，相率歸誠；

translations.literal: When troops arrive, they submit in groups;
translations.idiomatic: When troops arrive, they submit in groups;

sentences.zh: 兵退，復出焚掠。

translations.literal: when troops withdraw, they come out again to burn and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: when troops withdraw, they emerge again to burn and plunder.

sentences.zh: 層巒疊嶂，我師轉運為艱。

translations.literal: Layer upon layer of peaks and ridges—our army's transport is arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Layer upon layer of peaks and ridges make supply for our armies arduous.

sentences.zh: 夷族因利伺隙，倏起★L1伏，使我猝不及防。

translations.literal: The Yi tribes seize advantage and watch for openings, rising suddenly and striking and then hiding, so that we are caught unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Yi tribes seize advantage and watch for openings, rising suddenly to strike and then vanishing, catching us unprepared.

sentences.zh: 國家既厚集兵力，自當掃穴犁庭，除惡務盡，使諸夷望風震懾，一勞永逸。

translations.literal: Since the state has already massed troops in strength, it should naturally sweep the nests and plow the courts, eliminate evil to the utmost, and make all Yi tribes tremble at the wind in awe—a plan for one effort and lasting ease.
translations.idiomatic: Since the state has already massed its forces, it should sweep their nests, root out evil to the last man, and make all Yi tribes tremble at our might—a lasting settlement in one effort.

sentences.zh: 自古馭夷之法，討伐易而安撫難。

translations.literal: From antiquity the method of governing Yi: punitive campaigns are easy while pacification is hard.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity the method of governing Yi has been that punitive campaigns are easy while pacification is hard.

sentences.zh: 善後之舉，至要者二：一曰除內奸。

translations.literal: In measures for subsequent order, the most important are two: first, eliminate internal traitors.
translations.idiomatic: In measures for subsequent order, two points are paramount. First, eliminate internal traitors.

sentences.zh: 遊手無業之徒，潛居夷地，為之謀主，教以掠人勒贖，聚眾焚殺，及避火器敵官軍之策。

translations.literal: Idle men without occupation lurk in Yi territory and serve as their strategists, teaching them to seize people for ransom, gather crowds to burn and kill, and strategies to avoid fire-arms and oppose government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Idle men without occupation lurk in Yi territory and serve as their strategists, teaching them to seize people for ransom, gather mobs to burn and kill, and tactics to evade firearms and oppose government troops.

sentences.zh: 夷悍而愚，得之乃如虎傅翼，必應名捕，盡法懲治。

translations.literal: The Yi are fierce yet stupid; gaining such men is like adding wings to a tiger—they must be arrested by name and punished to the full extent of the law.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi are fierce yet simple. Gaining such men is like giving a tiger wings. They must be arrested by name and punished to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 良民亦驅使回籍，毋任逗留異域；

translations.literal: Good common people should also be driven to return to their native places and not be allowed to linger in foreign regions;
translations.idiomatic: Honest commoners should also be driven back to their native places and not allowed to linger in foreign regions;

sentences.zh: 宣諭土司，不得容留漢民；

translations.literal: proclaim to the native chieftains that they must not harbor Han commoners;
translations.idiomatic: native chieftains should be instructed that they must not harbor Han commoners;

sentences.zh: 營伍邏詰，絕其潛入之路，則奸人無繇扌冓煽矣。

translations.literal: garrisons should patrol and cut off their secret paths of entry—then traitors would have no means to incite and stir.
translations.idiomatic: garrisons should patrol and cut off secret paths of entry—then traitors would have no means to incite trouble.

sentences.zh: 一曰分疆界。

translations.literal: Second, divide territorial boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Second, divide territorial boundaries.

sentences.zh: 夷族愚惰，不諳農事，漢民租地，耕作有年，既漸闢磽鹵為膏腴，群夷涎其收穫，复思奪歸，構釁之原，不外於此。

translations.literal: Yi tribes are stupid and lazy and do not understand agriculture; Han commoners rent land and after years of cultivation gradually open barren salt wastes into fertile fields; the Yi tribes covet their harvests and again think to seize them back—the origin of provocation is nothing outside this.
translations.idiomatic: Yi tribes are dull and indolent and do not understand farming. Han commoners rent land and, after years of cultivation, gradually turn barren ground into fertile fields. Yi tribes covet the harvest and seek to seize the land back—the root of conflict lies here.

sentences.zh: 今當勘丈清釐，凡漢民屯種夷地，強佔者勒令退還，佃種者悉令贖歸。

translations.literal: Now we should survey and measure and clarify: wherever Han commoners have colonized and planted on Yi land, those who seized by force should be ordered to return it; those who rented should all be made to redeem and return.
translations.idiomatic: Surveys should now clarify boundaries: wherever Han have colonized Yi land, those who seized by force must return it; tenants must redeem and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 無主之田，墾荒已久，聚成村落，未便遷移，畫為漢界，禁​​其再行侵占，庶爭端永息。」

translations.literal: Land without owners that has long been reclaimed and gathered into villages cannot conveniently be moved; mark it as Han territory and forbid further encroachment—then disputes may cease forever."
translations.idiomatic: Unowned land long reclaimed and gathered into villages cannot conveniently be moved. Mark it as Han territory and forbid further encroachment, and disputes may cease."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「越巂廳設撫民通判，止治漢民，而熟夷皆受治土司，通判無專責，且營伍非其所轄，呼應不靈，每以細故釀為大釁。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The Yuexi subprefecture establishes a subprefect to pacify the people, who governs only Han commoners, while the mature Yi are all under native chieftains; the subprefect has no exclusive responsibility, and moreover garrisons are not under his jurisdiction—response is not nimble, and every small matter brews into a great provocation.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "At Yuexi Subprefecture the pacification subprefect governs only Han commoners, while mature Yi fall under native chieftains. The subprefect lacks exclusive authority, and garrisons are outside his jurisdiction, so coordination fails and small incidents brew into major conflicts.

sentences.zh: 請改為撫夷通判，千把總以下皆受節制。」

translations.literal: He requested that the title be changed to subprefect for pacifying the Yi, and that company commanders and platoon leaders and below all be under his control."
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the post be renamed subprefect for pacifying the Yi, with company commanders and platoon leaders and below all under his command."

sentences.zh: 疏上，下鄂山議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, it was sent down to E Shan for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to E Shan for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢工部侍郎，連典順天鄉試及會試。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to vice minister of Works and presided in succession over the Shuntian provincial examination and the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was promoted to vice minister of Works and presided in succession over the Shuntian provincial and metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 he died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宣宗最重文學廉謹之臣，辛從益直言獻納，張鱗廉介絕俗，沈維鐈服膺理學，程恩澤博物冠時，皆負清望。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The Xuanzong Emperor most valued literary, incorrupt, and careful ministers; Xin Congyi spoke frankly and offered counsel, Zhang Lin was pure and aloof beyond the common, Shen Weiqiao embraced Neo-Confucian learning, Cheng Enze was the foremost scholar of his age in breadth of learning—all bore clear reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary states: Emperor Xuanzong most valued literary, incorrupt, and careful ministers. Xin Congyi spoke frankly in counsel, Zhang Lin was upright beyond the common run, Shen Weiqiao embraced Neo-Confucian learning, and Cheng Enze was unrivaled in breadth of learning—all enjoyed clear reputations.

sentences.zh: 顧皋、朱為弼、吳杰並以雅材迴翔卿貳，亦足紀焉。

translations.literal: Gu Gao, Zhu Weibi, and Wu Jie all with elegant talent moved among vice-ministerial ranks, and are also worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Gao, Zhu Weibi, and Wu Jie all moved among vice-ministerial ranks with elegant talent, and are also worth recording.
